comm-prepare-browser-check.SKILL.md:
---
name: comm-prepare-browser-check
description: Use when preparing or diagnosing application browser-check conditions, including prototype previews; excludes harness validation.
---

# Establish browser conditions

Inputs: scenario, revision/resources, environment, authority.
Reuse valid evidence; recheck changed/unverified conditions.
Before the relevant actions read:
- Version/serving/preview: [artifacts](references/artifacts.md).
- Cache/storage/theme/viewport: [state](references/state.md).
- Session/process allocation/cleanup: [lifecycle](references/lifecycle.md).
- Navigation/data/API/observation: [preconditions](references/preconditions.md).

Use project tools; choices/gaps use comm-choose-effective-solution. Preserve
startup/check/permission/evidence owners; no implicit installation, repair or
cleanup of others' resources.

Done: actual conditions/evidence or exact gaps. Setup failure alone proves no
product defect. Harness validation stays separate.
comm-prepare-browser-check.references/preconditions.md:
# Reached scenario

Check navigation errors, final URL and target state; allow expected redirects,
disclose unexpected ones. New/substantially changed probes need working-page,
navigation-failure and redirect controls; absence of exceptions is insufficient.

Apply existing fixture-quality requirements. Confirm relevant API status/content
and actual mode; fallback screens prove no primary scenario. Retain expected
refusals/degradation in negative tests.

Observation must not change conditions accidentally. Unless testing concurrency,
avoid diagnostics interfering with unfinished actions. Use appropriate project
access, not copied SQL/settings. General classification/repair retain their owners.
comm-prepare-browser-check.references/artifacts.md:
# Artifact identity

Identify intended revision/build and coherent JS/CSS/templates/assets. Verify
imports, serving roots and browser-loaded files; cwd/HEAD alone proves no
identity. Use suitable existing IDs/manifests, paths or fingerprints.

Comparisons account for all components affecting the contract; established
unchanged ones may be shared. Equal results alone prove neither source error
nor success. Record snapshot origin/version and intentional edits; difference
from latest does not invalidate an approved versioned reference.

Prototype: correct base paths/version URL; confirm critical assets load/apply,
not just HTTP success. Separate servers and a nested-path 404 are not universal.
Shared symptoms do not prove a launch fault.
comm-prepare-browser-check.references/lifecycle.md:
# Session resources

Isolate independent contexts/profiles and conflicting ports where used; reuse
processes when isolation holds. Preserve intentional scenario state. Respect
caller settings; report conflicts, do not take another session.

Track ownership. Check live runs before restarting. Bound waits; try normal
closure, then only necessary authorized termination of proven owned processes.
No broad-name kills or foreign-profile deletion. Retain evidence; clean only
owned temporaries. Artifact creation, check outcome and process exit are distinct.
comm-prepare-browser-check.references/state.md:
# Actual state

Establish relevant requested conditions; verify actual:
- Service worker/cache: identify participation. Fresh-load checks need fresh
  conditions; update/offline/cache tests retain required mechanisms. No
  unconditional unregister/clear.
- Storage: establish relevant keys/values; distinguish defaults from persistence.
  Do not reset between steps testing preservation.
- Theme: account for system preference/app overrides; check effective styles/state.
  Flags/media preference alone prove no applied theme.
- Viewport: measure actual page width/height, scale when material; window/mobile
  flags are insufficient.

Reset only necessary authorized test state, never user/other-run data automatically.
Mismatches leave the claimed scenario unverified; classify cause separately.
